Question: A year is a leap year if and only if the year number is divisible by \(400\) (such as \(2000\)) or is divisible by \(4\) but not by \(100\) (such as \(2012\)). The \(200\)th anniversary of the birth of novelist Charles Dickens was celebrated on February \(7,\) \(2012,\) a Tuesday. On what day of the week was Dickens born?
Solution:
Dickens was born on February \(7\), \(2012-200=1812\). To compare the weekdays, count the leap days between February \(7\), \(1812\) and February \(7\), \(2012\). The leap day in \(1812\) is included because it follows his birth date; the leap day in \(2012\) is excluded because it follows the anniversary.

The candidate leap years are \(1812,1816,\ldots,2008\). Their number is
\[
\frac{2008-1812}{4}+1=50.
\]
Of these, \(1900\) is not a leap year because it is divisible by \(100\) but not \(400\). The year \(2000\) remains included because it is divisible by \(400\). Thus the interval contains \(49\) leap days.

A year of \(365\) days contains \(52\) complete weeks and one extra day. The \(200\) years therefore advance the weekday by \(200\) days, with another \(49\) days from leap days. Since
\[
200+49=249=35\cdot7+4,
\]
the anniversary is four weekdays after the birth date. Counting back four days from Tuesday gives Monday, Sunday, Saturday, Friday. Dickens was born on \(\boxed{\text{Friday}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
